title: Pakistan Deploys Drones and Helicopters in Intensified Balochistan Operations
excerpt: Security forces killed at least seven militants in intelligence-based operations in Kharan district as Pakistan escalates its counterterrorism campaign against separatist groups.
body:
• Pakistan's security forces have intensified military operations in Balochistan's Kharan district, deploying drones, helicopters, and additional ground troops against Baloch separatist groups.
  • At least seven militants were killed in intelligence-based operations in Kharan, with security forces recovering weapons including RPG launchers, submachine guns, and IED components.
  • Pakistan designates all Baloch insurgent groups as "Fitna al-Hindustan," accusing India of sponsoring the militancy — a claim India has consistently denied.
  • Balochistan has seen a sharp escalation in violence through 2026, with over 200 militants and dozens of soldiers killed since a massive coordinated attack in late January.

Pakistan has escalated military operations in Balochistan's remote Kharan district, deploying drones, military helicopters, and additional troops in what officials describe as a sustained counterterrorism campaign against Baloch separatist groups. At least seven militants were killed in the latest intelligence-based operations, according to Pakistan's military media wing ISPR and reports from Dawn.

What Happened in Kharan

Security forces launched the operations after intelligence reports identified movement of militants linked to the banned Balochistan Liberation Army in the Kharan district. In two separate engagements, troops killed seven fighters and recovered a significant weapons cache, according to ISPR.

https://x.com/miryar_baloch/status/2088915023330766932

The recovered arsenal included two rocket-propelled grenade launchers, 14 RPG rockets, IED components, three submachine guns, and large quantities of ammunition, according to Balochistan Pulse. Officials said the recovery suggested the militants were planning further attacks in the region.

Two civilians were also shot dead in a related terror attack in the area, according to The Economic Times, underscoring the toll the insurgency takes on Balochistan's civilian population.

A Province Under Siege

Balochistan — Pakistan's largest but poorest province — has been gripped by an escalating cycle of violence throughout 2026. The year's deadliest episode came on January 31, when the BLA launched coordinated attacks across Quetta, Nushki, Kharan, Gwadar, and several other locations, storming schools, banks, and security installations in one of their largest operations ever.

The military responded with Operation Radd-ul-Fitna-1, deploying helicopters and drones to retake the desert town of Nushki after a three-day siege. By the time operations concluded in early February, Pakistan's military said 216 militants had been killed across the province, along with 22 security personnel and 36 civilians.

Since then, smaller but persistent attacks have continued. In July, 75 insurgents were killed in operations following a BLA assault on a police post near Mangi Dam that left nine officers dead and 18 abducted. The abducted officers were later found blindfolded and shot dead.

India Accusations and Diplomatic Fallout

Pakistan's government has designated all Baloch insurgent organizations under the umbrella label "Fitna al-Hindustan," accusing India's intelligence agency RAW of sponsoring, funding, and directing the insurgency. India has consistently and categorically denied these allegations.

"Relentless counter-terrorism campaign under vision Azm-e-Istehkam by Pakistan's security forces and law enforcement agencies will continue at full pace to eliminate the menace of foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country."

— ISPR statement

The accusations have added friction to already strained India-Pakistan relations, which deteriorated further during military tensions earlier in 2026. For the Indian diaspora, the Pakistan-India dynamic in Balochistan remains a closely watched geopolitical issue, particularly given its implications for regional stability and the strategic China-Pakistan Economic Corridor that runs through the province.

The Bigger Picture

Balochistan's insurgency is rooted in decades of grievances. The province is rich in natural resources — gold, copper, and natural gas — but its ethnic Baloch population remains among Pakistan's most marginalized. Separatist groups argue that Islamabad exploits the province's wealth while neglecting its development.

China's multibillion-dollar investment in the Gwadar deepwater port and related CPEC infrastructure has intensified the conflict, with militants viewing the projects as further exploitation of Baloch resources.

What's Next

ISPR said sanitization operations in Kharan are ongoing, with security forces seeking to eliminate remaining militants in the area. Analysts expect the cycle of attack and counteroperation to continue, with no political settlement in sight for Balochistan's long-running insurgency.
nri_angle: Pakistan's escalating counterterrorism operations and its repeated accusations of Indian involvement in Balochistan's insurgency add friction to already strained India-Pakistan relations, a dynamic closely watched by the Indian diaspora.
author: Diaspora Desk
